Definition: from G1909 and G846 and (the dative case singular of) a derivative of φώρ (a thief); in theft itself, i.e. (by analogy) in actual crime:--in the very act.
BiblicalUsage: Epautophoroi means in the very act — caught in theft itself, in the middle of the crime. The scribes and Pharisees bring the woman to Jesus with this word on their lips: she was taken in adultery, in the very act. The phrase is their charge, not the whole story.
TheologicalSignificance: The accusers wanted the act, not the woman, but Jesus saw the woman and answered the accusers instead of condemning her.
